prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals and commitments (2010)

Economy and public finances
- Eliminate most of the structural current budget deficit over a Parliament; create an independent Office for Budget Responsibility; emergency Budget within 50 days.
- Cut at least £6bn in-year from departmental waste; freeze most public-sector pay for one year (excluding the lowest paid); reduce MPs by around 10%; cut ministerial pay and Whitehall/quango costs.
- Modify planned National Insurance rises to reduce costs for employers and workers under a set threshold.
- Publish spending over £25,000 and senior salaries; strengthen financial management and transparency across government.
- Corporate tax reform: reduce main and small-company rates funded by simplifying reliefs; create an Office of Tax Simplification; improve competitiveness for multinationals and intellectual property.
- Boost SMEs: NIC holiday for new firms’ first 10 hires; automatic small business rate relief; target 25% of government procurement to SMEs; open procurement and break up large ICT contracts.

Banking and financial regulation
- Put the central bank in charge of prudential supervision; bank levy; curb risky bonus structures; promote competition; explore a “people’s bank bonus” on sell-downs; expand credit channels for SMEs.

Growth, skills and regional policy
- Support hi‑tech exports and R&D; strengthen STEM in schools; multi‑year science budgets.
- Create 400,000 apprenticeships/training places over two years; £2,000 bonus for SMEs hiring apprentices; new all‑age careers service; free up further education colleges.
- Superfast broadband via infrastructure sharing; consider licence fee support for hard‑to‑reach areas.
- Replace Regional Development Agencies with business‑led Local Enterprise Partnerships; allow councils to keep above‑average business-rate growth.

Welfare and work
- Single Work Programme with payment by results; reassess incapacity claims; earlier, tailored support; sanctions for refusal; community work for long‑term claimants.
- “Work for Yourself” loans and mentoring; consider ending the default retirement age; mandatory equal‑pay audits for offenders.

Immigration
- Annual limit on non‑EU economic migration; default transitional controls for new EU members; English requirement for spouses; tighten student visas, bonds for certain institutions.

Infrastructure and transport
- Start high‑speed rail linking London/Heathrow to Birmingham, then to Manchester/Leeds, and onward phases; oppose new runways at Heathrow/Stansted/Gatwick; link Heathrow to HS rail.
- Longer rail franchises, stronger passenger advocacy, and EV charging network; consult on a Fair Fuel Stabiliser; shift from fixed speed cameras to targeted safety measures.

Energy, climate, and environment
- Legally aim for 80% emissions cut by 2050; 10% cut in central government emissions in year one.
- Green Investment Bank; carbon price floor via levy reform; increase share of environmental taxes offset by other tax reductions.
- Smart grid/meters; no public subsidy for new nuclear; four CCS plants; offshore grid; marine energy parks; district heating; incentives for small‑scale generation.
- “Green Deal” home energy upgrades repaid from bill savings; clearer energy bills and tariff info.
- Protect habitats; Marine Conservation Zones; tree‑planting programme; illegal timber offence; reform CAP/CFP; supermarket ombudsman; science‑led badger control in bTB hotspots; move toward zero‑waste with pay‑to‑recycle incentives; flood‑risk measures.

Families, health, and education
- End “couple penalty” in tax credits; consider recognition of stable couples in the tax system; extend flexible working and shared parental leave; strengthen child‑focused marketing rules; refocus Sure Start on early intervention; 4,200 additional health visitors.
- NHS: real-terms funding rises; patient choice of any qualified provider at NHS prices; GP‑led commissioning; independent NHS board; reduce management costs; 24/7 urgent care and single non‑emergency number; halt forced closures of local A&E/maternity; more single rooms; Cancer Drugs Fund; new dentistry contract; integrated personal budgets for long‑term conditions; support for carers; voluntary social‑care insurance option.
- Schools: expand academies and allow new “free schools”; pupil premium for disadvantaged pupils; stricter discipline; higher entry standards for teacher training; expand Teach First/Troops to Teachers; phonics and age‑6 reading check; more rigorous exams including separate sciences; technical academies; protect special schools; intervention in persistent failure.

Crime, policing, and civil liberties
- Elected local policing leaders; monthly local crime data; cut police paperwork; tougher knife‑crime sentencing; overhaul alcohol licensing and below‑cost sales; early‑intervention sanctions for antisocial behaviour; dedicated Border Police Force.
- Prisons: expand capacity; earned release within set ranges; payment‑by‑results rehabilitation; abstinence‑based drug orders; earlier deportation of foreign prisoners.
- Scale back ID and central databases; tighter rules on data retention/DNA; reform criminal records and libel laws.

Constitution, devolution, and foreign policy
- Recall for MPs; tighter lobbying rules; donation caps subject to cross‑party agreement; public‑led petitions/debates; stronger backbench control of Commons time.
- “Referendum lock” on future EU power transfers or Euro entry; seek return of certain powers; sovereignty legislation; support an elected second chamber model.
- Implement Scottish finance/devolution changes; Welsh referendum on further powers; support NI institutions; English votes for English laws.
- National Security Council; Strategic Defence and Security Review; renew the nuclear deterrent; defence procurement reform; measures supporting service personnel and families.
- Overseas aid at 0.7% of national income by 2013 with transparency, results‑based funding, malaria focus, and emphasis on trade, property rights, and post‑conflict stabilisation.
